mainEntity.name: How much does a Volkswagen Sharan 2.0 TDI engine replacement cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: A Volkswagen Sharan 2.0 TDI engine replacement typically costs between £1,500 and £4,000 for a reconditioned unit, depending on engine code, generation, and condition. Used units start from around £800, while reconditioned units range from £1,500 to £3,800. Supply and fit adds approximately £520-£715 in labour for an independent specialist.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of injector failure in a Volkswagen Sharan 2.0 TDI?

acceptedAnswer.text: The most common signs of injector failure in a Volkswagen Sharan 2.0 TDI include rough idling, jerking on acceleration, reduced power, increased fuel consumption, and black smoke from the exhaust. In advanced cases, the engine may fail to start or run on fewer than four cylinders. The fuel system may become contaminated with metal particles if an injector fails catastrophically.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in a Volkswagen Sharan 2.0 TDI?

acceptedAnswer.text: Whether it's worth replacing the engine in a Volkswagen Sharan 2.0 TDI depends on the car's value and condition. For 7N Sharan 2.0 TDI values above £5,000, a reconditioned engine with a 12-month warranty usually makes financial sense. For older 7M Sharan 2.0 TDI cars under £3,000, a used engine or injector replacement may be more economical.

mainEntity.name: How long does a Volkswagen Sharan 2.0 TDI engine replacement take?

acceptedAnswer.text: A Volkswagen Sharan 2.0 TDI engine replacement typically takes 1-2 days for a specialist workshop. The 2.0 TDI is a relatively common engine, and most supply-and-fit bookings can be completed within a week of ordering. 4Motion versions may require additional time for drivetrain calibration.

mainEntity.name: What's the difference between the Sharan 2.0 TDI 140, 170, and 184?

acceptedAnswer.text: The difference is engine code, generation, and tuning specification. The Volkswagen Sharan 2.0 TDI 140 (BKD, BRT, CFFB) produces 140hp and was available across 7M and early 7N generations. The 2.0 TDI 170 (CFGB) produces 170hp and was offered from 2010-2013. The 2.0 TDI 184 (2016-2022) produces 184hp and is the most powerful factory option.

mainEntity.name: Where is the engine code on a Volkswagen Sharan 2.0 TDI?

acceptedAnswer.text: The Volkswagen Sharan 2.0 TDI engine code is found in two places: on a sticker in the spare wheel well or the inside cover of the service book, and stamped on the engine block near the transmission bell housing. The code is also listed on the vehicle's V5C registration document. Common Sharan 2.0 TDI codes include BKD, BRT, CFFA, CFFB, CFFE, CFGB, CFGC, CRVA, CUVA, CUVC, DFLA, DFLD, and DLTC.

historyTimeline.h2: Volkswagen Sharan 2.0 TDI - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The Volkswagen Sharan 2.0 TDI arrived in 2005 as an upgrade to the popular 1.9 TDI PD, offering more power and refinement for Volkswagen's seven-seat MPV. The 2.0 TDI has been offered across both generations - the 7M (1995-2010) and the 7N (2010-2022) - evolving from the earlier BKD and BRT pump-nozzle units through to EA188 and EA288 common-rail engines delivering up to 184PS in the latest 7N models.

milestones.description: 2.0 TDI BKD (140hp) introduced in first-generation Sharan 7M
2010 - BRT (140hp) code also offered in 7M models
Second-generation Sharan (7N) launches with EA188 common-rail engines: CFFA (136hp), CFFB (140hp), CFGB (170hp)
Facelift 7N models introduce EA288 engines: CRVA (150hp) and CUVA/CUVC (115hp)
184PS 2.0 TDI (from Golf GTD) joins range with 4Motion
Sharan production ends; 2.0 TDI remains in service across UK roads

historyTimeline.closingNote: Every engine fitted to the Volkswagen Sharan 2.0 TDI is covered below, with UK rebuilt pricing and known failure points.

commonProblems.h2: Volkswagen Sharan 2.0 TDI Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The Volkswagen Sharan 2.0 TDI is a capable family MPV engine, but it has well-documented failure points - particularly piezo injector failure on both 7M and early 7N units, DPF and EGR system issues on Euro 5/6 models, and timing chain tensioner wear. Rebuilt engines through EnginesMarket include upgraded components addressing the original failure point, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.h4: Piezo Injector Failure - "Why the Volkswagen Sharan 2.0 TDI Injectors Fail"
problems.affectedModels: Volkswagen Sharan 2.0 TDI (BKD, BRT, CFFA, CFFB, CFFE, CFGB, CFGC - all EA188 common-rail and earlier pump-nozzle units)
problems.rootCause: Piezo injectors in the Bosch CR system are sensitive to fuel quality and can fail internally. When an injector fails, the clamp bolt can stretch and the copper seal can be destroyed, leading to fuel system contamination and no-start conditions.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace failed injector; code new unit
repairOptions.longevity: Viable if only one injector has failed

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace all four injectors; full system flush
repairOptions.longevity: Recommended when multiple failures or high mileage
When injector failure has caused collateral damage

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical used Volkswagen Sharan 2.0 TDI ranges from approximately £2,000 for an early 7M example to over £10,000 for a recent low-mileage 7N model. For 7M Sharan 2.0 TDI values under £3,000, a used engine or single injector replacement typically makes more sense than a full rebuilt unit. For 7N values £5,000-£10,000, reconditioned/rebuilt usually justifies the premium via warranty and reliability.
problems.recommendation: Injector failure on a Sharan 2.0 TDI can be a "canary in the coal mine" - if one injector has failed, the others may follow. For high-mileage 7N units, replacing all four injectors with the fuel system flush is the safest approach. If injector failure has caused metal contamination in the fuel system, full engine replacement may be the only option.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt Volkswagen Sharan 2.0 TDI engine prices

problems.h4: DPF & EGR System Failure - "Why the Volkswagen Sharan 2.0 TDI Emissions System Fails"
problems.affectedModels: Volkswagen Sharan 2.0 TDI (Euro 5 CFFA/CFFB/CFGB, Euro 6 CFGC/CRVA/CUVA)
problems.rootCause: Short urban journeys prevent passive DPF regeneration, leading to blockage. The EGR valve and cooler become clogged with carbon, triggering limp mode and warning lights.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Chemical or off-car DPF clean; EGR valve removal and carbon blast
repairOptions.longevity: Buy time on a car you plan to sell; may recur

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: New DPF and EGR valve fitted; software reset
repairOptions.longevity: Permanent fix; viable for cars worth over £4,000
When combined with other failures (injectors, turbo)

problems.vehicleValueCheck: For 7M Sharan 2.0 TDI under £3,000, DPF/EGR repairs may approach the car's value. For 7N models £5,000+, replacement components are a worthwhile investment.
problems.recommendation: DPF and EGR issues are often the first sign of a Sharan 2.0 TDI being used predominantly for short urban journeys. If you're keeping the car, a new DPF and EGR at £700-£1,500 from a specialist is good value. If combined with injector problems, a rebuilt engine becomes the more sensible long-term investment.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt Volkswagen Sharan 2.0 TDI engine prices

problems.h4: Turbocharger & Boost Leak Issues - "Why the Volkswagen Sharan 2.0 TDI Loses Power"
problems.affectedModels: Volkswagen Sharan 2.0 TDI (all generations, particularly high-mileage units)
problems.rootCause: The 2.0 TDI's variable geometry turbocharger can suffer from sticking vanes (carbon buildup) or oil starvation. Boost leaks from cracked intercooler pipes are also common across the Sharan range.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Remove and clean turbo vanes; replace actuator if sticking
repairOptions.longevity: Effective if caught early; may not resolve mechanical wear

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: New or reconditioned turbo; oil supply check
repairOptions.longevity: When turbo has failed; viable for cars worth over £5,000
When turbo failure has caused collateral engine damage

problems.vehicleValueCheck: For a Sharan 2.0 TDI worth over £5,000, a new turbo is a worthwhile investment. For older 7M models, evaluate repair cost against vehicle value.
problems.recommendation: Before replacing the turbo, check for boost leaks - cracked intercooler pipes are a common and relatively cheap fix. If turbo failure is confirmed and the car is worth over £5,000, a reconditioned engine with warranty is often better value than paying for turbo replacement alone on a high-mileage unit.
